title: Neuroblastoma: treatment by risk group
alt: After INRG staging and biology, patients split three ways: low risk has surgery alone with chemotherapy only if symptomatic; intermediate risk has surgery plus 4 to 8 chemotherapy cycles and radiotherapy only for residual disease; high risk has induction chemotherapy, surgery, stem cell transplant, radiotherapy and dinutuximab with isotretinoin. Survival falls from over 95% to about 50–60%.
caption: Groups and treatment arms follow the COG/INRG risk classification; survival figures are approximate.

nodes.text: Newly diagnosed neuroblastoma: INRG stage, age, MYCN status, histology, ploidy, segmental aberrations
Low risk: stage L1, or L2 and MS with favourable biology
Surgery alone: gross total or partial resection; observe asymptomatic MS disease
Chemotherapy only for symptoms, progression or unresectable disease
Intermediate risk: L2 or M without MYCN amplification; symptomatic MS
Surgery plus 4 to 8 cycles of carboplatin, etoposide, cyclophosphamide and doxorubicin
Radiotherapy only for residual disease; no stem cell transplant
High risk: stage M over 18 months, MYCN amplified, or unfavourable L2
Induction chemotherapy 5 to 6 cycles, then resection of primary and metastases
Myeloablative chemotherapy with autologous stem cell transplant
Radiotherapy to the primary site and any residual disease
Dinutuximab with GM-CSF, then isotretinoin for 6 months
Survival about 50 to 60%; most relapses happen here
